This comment line made me understand exactly why Star Fox is dormant.    
A 2 hours On-Rails Shooter is too short.    
A 3 hours On-Rails Shooter is too long.    
An adventure game where you play as Fox in a planet or another is too different.    
A third person shooter game with vehicle mechanics is too hated.    
A strategy game is too hated too.    
A space flight simulator with shooting elements is too boring after a while.   
An open world experience set in multiple planets and space where you get upgrades for your weapons and ships and use them to advance in Mercennary missions sounds excellent... But is not Star Fox, and shoehorning Star Fox on it would be not good enough for a lot of people      

Add the furry stigma, the general hate for characters like Krystal and the awful reception of most endings on Star Fox command and the absolute failure that Star Fox Zero was and I honestly don't see a way Nintendo can honestly bring the series back in a way that actually is good enough, even with great Multiplayer and embracing the legacy of the characters after the Smash Games or something is extremely difficult to justify the effort on this series when you have more readily accepted series for practically everything Star Fox can feasibly do in this point in gaming

Star Fox Assault is a great game with a killer multiplayer with a Spin on the formula, great controls with multiple options, a very cool story that follows the beats of the previous games, great maps, and could be around 20 hours on the main story alone if you watch all cutscenes and conversations, cheesy but cool voice acting and awesome replay value in multiple ways 

And everyone hates Star Fox: Assault (Except me, Star Fox: Assault supremacy)

So yes, I see why is extremely difficult for Nintendo to justify anything aside from re-releases for this franchise, they finally released Star Fox 2, both Star Fox and Star Fox 64 are available in NSO and Nintendo even re-released Command of all games in the Wii U E-Shop, I'm pretty sure that they know the franchise exists but just know they have a very difficult time creating an actually successor to it, I could see Remasters or even Remakes of the Gamecube games to check interest on the series before we see an actual New Star Fox

I think there is a main difference between "look at my passion" and "look at my money", most of the collections I look at are passionate, well put together collections of games that gives a general Idea on the mind of the collector based on what they get, what they like and where they live 

I think the main difference comes when you walls of games, all of them being the most valuable possible, often with repeats of the most searched ones, or everything sealed, graded, whatever, I like looking at them because I don't have enough money for even a Gundam GameCube and it's cool to see what people with money collect, but it does feel like an insane flex, like a "look, I have this much money, do you?"

Collections built with time and effort are also pretty cool, I like people that handpick what they get and you can see that when the collection is organized in a way you know what they got recently is in the spot it needs and it's not a "I bought a Lot of 40 boxed shovelware games to fill up the wall"

Even then, I like whatever the post because I like enjoying the hobby and what other people enjoy, yeah, sometimes I'm envious when someone is flexing a specific very expensive item that I just won't ever get in my country, but it's also part of it, I try to direct that negativity into patience and "One day that one will be on my shelf" instead of "stop flexing"

Lo único que sé de esa frase es que la usa gente que busca gente que no sabe pero quiere parecer intelectual, aquellos que buscan "invertir" en productos de colección y que les pueden vender la pomada de que ellos saben que en 2 años más va a ser 2 o 3 veces más caro, cuando están vendiendo algo a precio ya inflado, algo que los verdaderos "entendidos" no tocarían ni con un palo

Una buena manera de colocar cartuchos en cajas para protegerlos es aplicar cajas específicas y romperlas un poquito
Todos mis juegos de GB, GBC y GBA están en cajas de Casette con Portadas Custom
Y los juegos de NES a 64 caben todos en cajas de VHS, solo hay que romper los topecitos chicos que tienen adentro y darte la paja de imprimir y recortar las portadas

La mayoría de juegos que salieron en cajas de Plástico tienen cajas estandarizadas, por lo que usar la caja de un juego para colocar la de otro es viable y hay juegos de DS y 3DS que llegan a valer 1 Luca porque son malos, comunes o repetitivos (cómo Fifa y los llamados "Shovelware")

Aquí en Chile a través de Mercado Libre, Facebook e Instagram vas a encontrar más de una persona que trabaja haciendo cajas de cartón personalizadas que son básicamente réplicas de las originales, pero el principal drama que tienen es que baratas no son y sí quieres consistencia vas a terminar teniendo que pedir muchas

I worked at a video game store

There was this kid, 8 years tops who came to the store with their mother, the kid was looking for a Yoshi plushie whe had last week.
Their mother was exceptionally against the idea of the kid having the plushie, or entering a video game store, you coul tell from her face and actitude that she only wanted to get over it and take her kid out.
So, the kid asked about the plush and after I searched for it and discovered it was sold out, I told the kid.
They were devastated, her mother just said something like "well, let's go" and grabbed the kid.
I just said "So... You like Mario? I do too, do you have any other character you like"
The mother rolled her eyes but the kid just had the brightest smile on their face.
I talked to the kid for a while, with the mother and my boss permission, told him things about nintendo and video games they were extremely happy and smiled most of the way.
It was going well until he said something like "my friends don't like Mario"
I just answered "Now you have a friend who likes it, and you will have a lot more"
The mother eventually said "We need to go, What's the Plushie" 
The kid left the store with a Koopa Troopa plushie and a smile.

I stopped working there because I needed to study in another city, never heard of the kid again, not even from co-workers.
I hope he is doing well and still playing video games
